Snitkiv Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Snitkiv's Jewish community, present from the early 18th century and surviving Haidamak attacks in the 1730s, reached 1,126 people (39 percent of the town) by 1897. In 1913, the community supported a branch of the Zionist HeHalutz movement, training members for agricultural settlement in the Land of Israel. After the German occupation of July 1941, Jewish houses were marked with Stars of David and residents forced to wear them; Bessarabian Jews were later brought into the resulting ghetto, and able-bodied workers were sent to the Letychiv labor camp, documented elsewhere in this collection, before most of Snitkiv's Jews were killed in August and October 1942.
